theme: I give you thanks with my whole heart
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 138. David gives thanks with his whole heart. Notice that his praise is directed to the LORD before other gods, and that it is based on God’s steadfast love, his faithfulness, and his answer to prayer.
settingTheScene: Psalm 138 begins a final group of psalms by David (138 to 145). It is a thanksgiving psalm, offered in response to an answered prayer. David praises God “before the gods,” that is, in the presence of the pagan powers and idols, and expects that all the kings of the earth will join. It echoes the Prison Epistles’ theme that Christ is exalted above all powers.
observation: “I give you thanks, O LORD, with my whole heart; before the gods I sing your praise” (v. 1).
“For you have exalted above all things your name and your word” (v. 2).
“On the day I called, you answered me; my strength of soul you increased” (v. 3).
“All the kings of the earth shall give you thanks, O LORD” (v. 4).
“For though the LORD is high, he regards the lowly” (v. 6).
“Though I walk in the midst of trouble, you preserve my life” (v. 7).
“The LORD will fulfill his purpose for me; your steadfast love, O LORD, endures forever” (v. 8).
“Do not forsake the work of your hands” (v. 8).
interpretation:
The psalm begins with wholehearted praise. David refuses to give thanks halfway. He sings “before the gods,” which probably refers to the gods of the nations or the heavenly powers. Even in the presence of rivals, he praises the LORD. He bows toward the holy temple and gives thanks to God’s name “for your steadfast love and your faithfulness, for you have exalted above all things your name and your word.” God’s name is his revealed character, and his word is his promise. Both are supremely reliable.

Verse 3 is a testimony: “On the day I called, you answered me; my strength of soul you increased.” The answer was not necessarily the removal of trouble but strength within it. The effect of God’s answer extends outward: “All the kings of the earth shall give you thanks, O LORD, for they have heard the words of your mouth, and they shall sing of the ways of the LORD, for great is the glory of the LORD.” David’s experience of God’s faithfulness is a testimony to the nations. This is a missionary note. One day, kings will sing the praises of the LORD.

Verse 6 holds a great truth: “For though the LORD is high, he regards the lowly, but the haughty he knows from afar.” God is exalted, and yet he looks on the humble. The proud cannot approach him. This is the theme of the Christ hymn in Philippians 2. The one who humbled himself is now exalted, and God looks on those who humble themselves.

David then expresses trust in future danger: “Though I walk in the midst of trouble, you preserve my life; you stretch out your hand against the wrath of my enemies, and your right hand delivers me.” The key promise is verse 8: “The LORD will fulfill his purpose for me.” This echoes Philippians 1:6: he who began a good work will bring it to completion. God’s purposes for us cannot be thwarted. Based on God’s steadfast love that endures forever, David prays, “Do not forsake the work of your hands.” It is a prayer of confidence, not doubt: because God has made us and begun a work in us, we ask him to finish it.
connection: Philippians 1:6 and Psalm 57:2 speak of God fulfilling his purpose. Psalm 100 and 136 emphasize steadfast love. Psalm 72:11 and 102:15 speak of kings worshiping. Isaiah 57:15 says God dwells with the contrite and lowly. James 4:6 and 1 Peter 5:5 say God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble. Luke 1:48-52 is Mary’s song of the lowly lifted. Jeremiah 29:11 speaks of God’s plans. Revelation 21:24-26 pictures kings bringing glory into the city. Ephesians 2:10 speaks of us as God’s workmanship.
application:
Give thanks to God today with your whole heart, with no reservations.

Recall a day you called and he answered. Tell it to someone.

Pray verse 8 over a project or relationship: LORD, fulfill your purpose here.
prayerPrompts: Give God thanks with your whole heart, naming something.
Thank him that he exalted his word above his name.
Ask him to complete what he has begun in you.
